steps.what: Describe the requested client appointment and available times
Clarify the service and duration needed for the client appointment
Compare appointment requirements with staff and resource calendar availability
Enter the proposed appointment with the correct service and client details
Check and read back the complete appointment, service, price terms and contact details
Confirm the exact client appointment and confirmation destination
Reserve the confirmed client appointment in the actual agenda
Send the exact appointment confirmation to the confirmed client destination

tasks.design: Configure native service-duration and availability checks in the salon booking tool {OTHER}, with linked {CALENDAR} availability and reusable client fields. The stylist clarifies the service, reads back the complete proposal and reserves and confirms only the exact appointment accepted by the client.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual slot comparison and repeated client and service entry surround telephone bookings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native resource checks and client-linked forms handle the fixed scheduling work without a conversational agent.
tasks.still_hard: A new service may need a consultation before its duration and suitability are known.
tasks.human_edge: Clarify what the client wants and avoid an unsuitable or rushed service slot.

ambition.what: The stylist keeps service suitability and booking responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native salon calendars can compare service durations and resource availability and reuse client fields while service clarification remains human.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual assisted booking including client participation, reservation and its real confirmation. This is not a claim that client self-service is free; customer shares remain fully retained and excluded from the stylist denominator.

Salon management maintains service code, duration, price terms and qualified staff; calendar owners maintain availability. The client supplies needs in s1; the stylist captures details in s4. Missing or incompatible availability needs funded manual repair.
s3 replaces actual manual slot comparison. s4 removes ten units of repeated client and service fields, retaining ten for changed details and checks. Native functions already used earn no new saving.

Reservation and confirmation keep their full current time, so no save or send runtime benefit is claimed. s6 is the client's actual acceptance of the complete appointment and exact contact destination; any changed time, service, terms or contact requires renewed acceptance. Internal draft saving is negligible and ungated.
unknowns: How much manual comparison remains in the current salon agenda
Whether the service needs a prior consultation
research_questions: Can duration and resource checks reject an overlapping appointment while preserving the client's exact acceptance?

incremental.description: Maintain service durations and repair missing availability or client-field mappings

steps.what: Capture the actual beauty service details and read completed checkout facts
Copy completed service, product and fee facts into the draft customer card
Check customer card fields against the actual beauty services and correct mismatches
Write and check actual customer formula and preference details in the card
Save the customer card in its existing salon screen

tasks.design: Reuse completed checkout facts as draft card fields in the salon records tool {OTHER}, using native links before custom integration. The stylist captures the real treatment, verifies the assembled facts and writes the actual formula or preference notes before an ordinary ungated save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checkout facts are manually copied into a separate client card.
tasks.enabler_now: A deterministic native link can reuse actual completed transaction fields without a model.
tasks.still_hard: The exact formula, response and preference must reflect what happened, not a planned service.
tasks.human_edge: Remember and verify the practical details needed for the next safe and consistent visit.

ambition.what: The stylist keeps responsibility for accurate treatment history.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: completed checkout facts can populate client-card drafts deterministically, while actual treatment details require stylist capture and checking.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing salon checkout and client-record tools. Boundary is the actual card used at later visits, not a new post-visit report or client message.

Checkout staff produce client id, service code, product code and fee through the actual completed sale, which is a separate workflow. s1 counts the stylist's real treatment capture and checkout-fact checking; it does not assume the booked service proves completion.

s2 replaces actual manual copying only where native checkout-to-card reuse is absent. Missing links or failed conversions stop for funded manual repair. s4 removes1.5 units of repeated formula field labels, retaining13.5 for actual values and checks.

The machine creates draft fields rather than releasing a financial or treatment decision. Ordinary author save is tiny, fully retained and ungated; no self-approval is added. Any sensitive health detail needs the operator's actual lawful access and collection route, not inferred data.
unknowns: Whether checkout already updates the client card
Which treatment details are actually needed and recorded
research_questions: Can the card distinguish completed checkout facts from changed treatment details?

already_counted.description: Capture treatment facts, verify assembled fields, write actual formula details and save

incremental.description: Repair mismatched client and service references and maintain checkout-to-card fields

tasks.short: Assess hair and recommend a suitable treatment

steps.what: Read the patron's existing beauty treatment history before consultation
Examine hair condition and physical features directly
Discuss maintenance needs and recommend beauty treatment or hair styles

tasks.design: Show the existing treatment history in a concise native client-card view in {OTHER} before the consultation. The stylist examines the hair and physical features and discusses suitable treatment and maintenance directly with the patron.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant existing treatment facts may be scattered across the client card.
tasks.enabler_now: A configured view can reduce screen navigation without replacing inspection or advice.
tasks.still_hard: Hair condition, suitability and the patron's practical preferences require direct assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Combine physical examination with a candid discussion of what the patron can maintain.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: client-card views can bring existing treatment facts together, but hair and feature assessment requires direct stylist examination.

assumptions: OTHER means the salon client-card tool and physical consultation tools. Boundary ends with advice; booking, actual treatment and the real client-record update are separate tasks.

The existing card contains facts already captured by the treating stylist. No new questionnaire, record, image analysis or report is assumed. If no history is used today, this small navigation opportunity is absent.
s1 removes two units of screen navigation and retains eight for reading. The examination and live advice retain their full time; the card view makes no suitability decision.
unknowns: Whether the stylist already sees a concise treatment history
research_questions: Does the current card require navigation that can be removed without hiding relevant treatment facts?

already_counted.description: Read history, examine the patron and give the actual recommendation

incremental.description: Maintain the history view and resolve missing display fields

tasks.short: Develop practical new styles and techniques

steps.what: Browse relevant styles and techniques as starting references
Try new styles and techniques using actual hair and styling tools
Evaluate the styles and refine techniques for practical repeatability

tasks.design: Use a native filtered view of the stylist's existing reference collection in {OTHER} to shorten browsing. Physical trials and evaluation remain with the stylist because a reference image does not establish a workable technique.
tasks.previous_blocker: Browsing an unfiltered existing style collection can take time before practical experimentation starts.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing collection filters can narrow references by the stylist's chosen technique and hair characteristics.
tasks.still_hard: A new technique must work with real tools, hair texture and repeatable movements.
tasks.human_edge: Develop practical judgement through physical experimentation and refinement.

ambition.what: The stylist remains the technique developer.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: filtered reference collections can shorten browsing, while developing a repeatable hair technique still requires physical trials.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing style-reference collection and physical styling tools. This boundary contains no invented development report, publication or client treatment record.
Existing reference publishers supply the collection metadata. The stylist chooses the goal and relevant references in s1; no new tagging or content collection is assumed free.
s1 removes1.5 units of unrelated browsing while retaining13.5 for visual selection. Trials60 and evaluation25 remain fully retained. Native filtering already in use earns no new benefit.
unknowns: Whether existing collection filters meaningfully distinguish the desired technique
research_questions: Can current reference metadata narrow browsing without excluding useful styles?

already_counted.description: Select references, perform physical trials and refine the technique

incremental.description: Maintain the chosen reference view and repair unsuitable filters

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R98.5 gross1.5 less upkeep0.5 gives1. For styles with poor reference metadata, selection retains14.5 of15 while trials60 and evaluation25 remain; gross0.5 is consumed by upkeep0.5. The estimate concerns existing browsing only, with no invented administrative baseline.
